summary: One pull request in eight ordered tasks: pure split/align/carry and UTF-16 offsets in packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/itemblocks; migrations for comment_blocks, message_blocks, comment_block_texts, owed state rows with triggers, item block refs, replies_to_block columns and six graph_edges arms under storage kinds comment_block/message_block; IndexItem at every comment and message write and in ReindexOwedItem; the item-block reference grammar and graph readers (API node kind block, R12 facts, pins on comment revisions); reply_to_block / in_reply_to_block with reply_block on every read and event; GET /api/v1/comments/{id}/blocks and /messages/{id}/blocks and dispatch read of an item block; the dashboard comment editor carrying block ids through edits; rebuild-refs, the block-index loop's third batch, the driver's A7/A10/A11/A13/A15-comment sections, two Conversation tab browser rows, docs and five changelogs.

implement: legion-worker: phase rules, push and handoff, and references/pr-body.md for proof entries, the census and the simplify pass (references/conflicts-and-rewrites.md if #2394 or #2245 merges first and a migration renumber or view restatement conflicts)
ce-simplify-code: the simplify pass the PR body reference requires on settled code before the proof head
dispatch: the production record and any Dispatch write (the plan's after-merge production check writes the Production line and reads threads with dispatch read)
test: legion-worker: the tester's evidence rules and references/pr-body.md for what a proof is; re-run the plan's driver, Playwright and Go commands at the head on the local harness
dispatch: reading threads and references with dispatch read on the harness and checking the CLI output the plan names
review: legion-worker: references/merge-gate.md for review and approval of the head, and references/review-threads.md for threads
ce-simplify-code: judge whether the new itemblocks, refs/item_blocks.go and block-spans.ts code is as simple as its rules allow

findings.finding: Reusing block_grammar_owed lets an older build drain the queue without indexing blocks (old ReindexOwedItem deletes rows; old sourceText treats direct messages as gone).
findings.answer: Decision 7: owed_at on comment_block_state and message_block_state, set by new triggers the older build does not know; drained only by this build's block-index tick as a third batch under the existing lease. Rollback leaves items owed for the next roll forward.

findings.finding: On ?to=<target>, is a comment mention's source the block node or the comment (R7 vs R14 and the driver's existing checks)?
findings.answer: Decision 4: the block node with parent the comment, as documents do; every reader that renders a source (ReferencedBy.tsx groups by parent, dispatch-execute.ts referenceLines/blockLines) is updated and listed in a census; the driver's existing source checks move to the block node with parent.id the comment.

findings.finding: Counts: older builds double-count block rows during the roll; the two-paragraph count changes; event counted changes can miss a link moving between blocks.
findings.answer: Decision 2: storage kinds comment_block/message_block, which an older build skips as unknown (no double count, rollback-safe). Two paragraphs citing one target count 2, once counts 1 (TestAMentionStartsAtItsBlock). IndexItem returns targets whose block rows changed for the event's counted changes.

findings.finding: Direct-message mentions would become visible on public ?to= reads.
findings.answer: Decision 4: a direct message writes no block mentions (as it writes no mentions today); its blocks are nodes reachable only through the blocks route under getMessageThread's read check.

findings.finding: Stale or owed items: the blocks route would hand the editor wrong ids; replies to an unindexed block are refused.
findings.answer: The blocks route answers indexed:false with no blocks when owed or the body hash differs, and writes nothing; the editor then sends no ids. A reply naming a block of an owed parent indexes the parent first in its own transaction, under the lock it already holds.

findings.finding: Writes during the roll: an older pod refuses the new fields and has no blocks routes.
findings.answer: Decision 13: the save fails with the older pod's 400, the draft stays, the person saves again; no retry logic. Transient and lossless.

findings.finding: Editor offsets vs the trim and CR LF (a textarea turns CR LF into LF).
findings.answer: Decisions 6 and 8: offsets are UTF-16 over the stored body, translated by the composer into the textarea value; the trim shift is applied before sending; the identity hash reads CR LF as LF, so a line-ending-only change moves nothing.
Decision 10: any reply in an ask's thread (ask_id, or reply_to whose thread head is an ask) naming a block is refused 400 INVALID_COMMENT until INFRA-369.

findings.finding: A13 restore: rule 2 matches only the removed block's last text; Backspace deletion holds no span.
findings.answer: Restore means the text that was deleted, matched against the removed block's last text (rule 2) on a later save; within one edit, cut/drag holds the span and paste/drop of the same text returns it. Documented in the AGENTS paragraph.

findings.finding: PR #2394 also restates graph_edges; can a block[] attribute name a comment block?
findings.answer: The second to merge carries both sets of arms; block[] points at document blocks only, with a refusal test if #2394 is on main at implementation, else an Envoy message to the root's implementer before review ends.

findings.finding: Migration census, seed conflicts, locks named in the README, and lock order.
findings.answer: Seeds use on conflict do nothing; census answers 0; README names ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on comments, messages, graph_edges and SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE per trigger migration; lock order owner, item, state, and the reconciler never takes an owner row.

findings.finding: R12 made_at for blocks is unspecified (tree plan said made_at = changed_at).
findings.answer: Decision 12: made_at is the revision that first held the block; null for a block found at the first indexing of a comment edited before this change; message block made_at is created_at; parent_version changed_revision for comments, null for messages.

findings.finding: Machine checks for A7, A10, A11, A13, A15-comment, R12 replies, R14; A13/A15 cannot run in production (human-only PATCH, no dev sign-in).
findings.answer: Each has a driver section and a Go test with the concrete assertions; the driver's new optional DEV_SIGNIN_LOGIN input runs A13/A15-comment on the harness and prints SKIP lines on production, where the browser rows are the proof (recorded as a spec departure).

specDepartures.spec: Issue spec, second R11 bullet: block ids survive every edit 'through the dashboard and through an agent's command', and 'A13 now also splits the cited paragraph and edits through an agent's command'.
specDepartures.plan: No agent command edits a comment. The dashboard editor carries ids (PATCH with blocks and base_revision); an API body without ids is matched by the five text rules.
specDepartures.evidence: Root spec R11 at approved version 16 says only the dashboard editor carries ids and an API body is text-matched; architect comment dispatch://INFRA-368/comment/35191e49-42d2-4242-8e16-b8b77361c1e4 says no new agent command is in scope and A13's edits go through the dashboard editor.

acceptance: A13 as worded in the issue spec's second R11 bullet: its edits run through the dashboard editor (and the editor's PATCH wire in the driver), not an agent's command.

specDepartures.spec: Issue spec, Proof: the driver's A7 section, extended with A10 and A13, runs through the real CLI and HTTP on the local harness before the merge and on production after it.
specDepartures.plan: On production the driver's A13 and A15-comment sections print a SKIP line naming why; they run on the local harness with the new optional DEV_SIGNIN_LOGIN input, and the browser rows prove them before the merge.
specDepartures.evidence: PATCH /api/v1/comments/{id} is authHuman (packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/routes_table.go:142, comment_actions.go:134-137) and production has no dev sign-in; the deployment instructions say a path only a person can take is proven by the browser test and nothing else.

outcome.scope: The production run proves A7, A10 and A11 for comment and message blocks; A13 and the comment half of A15 are proven before the merge only, by the browser rows and the harness run.

specDepartures.spec: Issue spec: plan from the tree plan's PR5 section (Task 5.2 storage, Task 5.7 first-hour sweep under an item-blocks lease, contract item 13 node kind block).
specDepartures.plan: Storage kinds comment_block and message_block in graph_edges and refs.to_kind (the API node stays kind block); owed_at state with triggers drained by the existing block-index loop, no new lease and no first-hour sweep.
specDepartures.evidence: An older build counts every 'block' row in BacklinkCounts and resolves it through document_blocks (refs/graph.go:61-95, 296-312), and its ReindexOwedItem would drain a shared queue without indexing blocks (refs/rebuild.go:154, 211-247); the lease pool has no headroom (store/pool.go:258-274).

specDepartures.spec: Tree plan PR5 (which the issue spec says to plan from): item ids aligned by five text rules on every edit, a split or join mints new ids, no pin storage for comments, made_at = changed_at, reply_to_block refused only with ask_id.
specDepartures.plan: Carried ids from the editor with split-keeps-start and join-keeps-first; comment_block_texts for pins at a comment revision; made_at the revision that first held the block; any reply in an ask's thread refused a block; identity hash reads CR LF as LF; direct messages write no block mentions; the blocks route adds from, to (UTF-16) and indexed.
specDepartures.evidence: Root spec v16 R1, R11, R12 and A13, A15; the issue spec's bullets superseding 'Item mentions stay on the item' and the split/join rule; messages.go:184 (direct messages write no mentions today); a textarea turns CR LF into LF.
